subsystems.name: Quantum sensor element
subsystems.role: converts tiny magnetic or electric fields from biomarkers into a measurable quantum state change.

subsystems.name: Excitation and control
subsystems.role: initialises and manipulates the quantum state for sensing.

subsystems.name: Magnetic shielding
subsystems.role: suppresses Earth's magnetic field and ambient noise so femtotesla-scale biomagnetic signals can be detected.

subsystems.name: Readout
subsystems.role: measures the quantum state after exposure to the biomarker signal.

subsystems.name: Sample interface
subsystems.role: brings the biomarker into close proximity with the sensor.
parts: functionalised sensor surface with antibodies or aptamers

subsystems.name: Data acquisition and analysis
subsystems.role: extracts the diagnostic signal from noise and converts it into a clinical result.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the quantum sensor
buildSteps.detail: Grow diamond with controlled nitrogen-vacancy centres, or build a sealed atomic vapour cell, or pattern a superconducting loop with Josephson junctions.

buildSteps.title: Functionalise the sensor surface
buildSteps.detail: Attach antibodies, aptamers or other capture molecules that bind only the target biomarker, so it is held within nanometres of the sensor.

buildSteps.title: Assemble excitation and control optics
buildSteps.detail: Align lasers, microwave waveguides and coils to initialise and manipulate the quantum state reliably.

buildSteps.title: Integrate magnetic shielding
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the sensor in mu-metal and add active coils to cancel the remaining ambient field, since biomagnetic signals are around a millionth of Earth's field.

buildSteps.title: Build the readout chain
buildSteps.detail: Connect photodetectors or microwave electronics to low-noise amplifiers and digitizers that capture the quantum state.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate with known samples
buildSteps.detail: Measure known concentrations of the biomarker to establish a dose–response curve and detection limit.

buildSteps.title: Validate in clinical studies
buildSteps.detail: Test on patient samples against existing diagnostic methods to prove sensitivity, specificity and reproducibility.

prerequisites.why: nitrogen-vacancy diamond and atomic vapours are demonstrated in labs, but reproducible, high-yield fabrication is still maturing.
SQUIDs already detect biomagnetic fields down to femtotesla, and optically pumped magnetometers now do so at room temperature.
antibodies and aptamers can selectively bind disease markers, though attaching them without degrading the sensor is challenging.
no quantum sensor diagnostic for molecular biomarkers has yet passed regulatory trials for routine clinical use.
optically pumped magnetometers and diamond sensors work without cryogenics, but achieving SQUID-level sensitivity in a compact device remains difficult.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of nitrogen-vacancy nanoscale NMR and optically pumped magnetometers for magnetoencephalography
pathway.unlocks: proof that quantum sensors can detect magnetic signals from biological samples and brain activity.

pathway.milestone: clinical pilots of quantum sensors for magnetocardiography and magnetoencephalography
pathway.unlocks: reliable, non-invasive functional imaging without cryogenic cooling.

pathway.milestone: in vitro diagnostic devices that detect specific protein or nucleic-acid biomarkers at low concentration
pathway.unlocks: earlier detection of diseases such as cancer or infections from blood samples.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval and point-of-care or implantable quantum diagnostic systems
pathway.unlocks: widespread screening and continuous monitoring at molecular sensitivity.
